blocks.orig: Lions are natural predators. In the wild, they must hunt for their food, and this is why they are usually at the top of the food chain.
blocks.html: By nature, lions are predators. Out in the wild they have to hunt to eat, which is what generally places them at the top of the food chain.

blocks.orig: While it can be difficult to think of these beautiful creatures as hunters, this is part of nature, and ultimately part of the great circle of life.
blocks.html: It can feel strange to picture such beautiful animals as hunters, yet this is simply how nature works and, in the end, part of the great circle of life.

blocks.orig: If you are visiting any African countries where lions reside, it is likely that you will want to do a game tour to see these creatures in their natural habitat.
blocks.html: Should you travel to any African country with a lion population, chances are you'll want to join a game tour and watch these animals in their own habitat.

blocks.orig: But you might be anxious about the chance of a lion attacking you during this tour.
blocks.html: At the same time, you may worry that a lion could attack you during such a tour.

blocks.orig: Read on to find out why lions do not attack tourists while they are on jeeps.

blocks.orig: Why Don’t Lions Attack Tourists On Jeeps?
blocks.html: Why don’t lions attack tourists in jeeps?

blocks.orig: It is incredibly unlikely for a lion to attack a tourist jeep during a game tour.
blocks.html: The odds of a lion going for a tourist jeep on a game tour are extremely small.

blocks.orig: While attacks have occurred in the past, they are incredibly rare, and this is why this style of tour is so popular.
blocks.html: Attacks have happened before, but they are exceptionally rare, and that is precisely why this type of tour remains so popular.

blocks.orig: The main reason why lions do not attack tourists on jeeps is because of the predator-prey instincts that keep lions alive in the wild.
blocks.html: The chief explanation lies in the predator-prey instincts that keep a lion alive in the wild: those same instincts stop it from attacking people in jeeps.

blocks.orig: While a single human being isn’t seen as a predator to a lion, and instead is seen as something they could easily attack, the same cannot be said for a jeep.
blocks.html: A lone human is not regarded as a predator by a lion; rather, it is something the lion could take down with ease. A jeep, however, is a different matter.

blocks.orig: Any motor vehicle that has 4-wheels is usually perceived as a threat by lions, simply due to the size of these vehicles.
blocks.html: Lions tend to perceive any four-wheeled motor vehicle as a threat, purely because of how big such vehicles are.

blocks.orig: But a jeep is seen as even more of a threat due to the large size of these vehicles.
blocks.html: A jeep, being larger still, comes across as an even greater threat.

blocks.orig: Jeeps are much larger than a single lion, and when you combine this with the number of human beings that a jeep can hold at once, it is easy to see why lions see jeeps as a threat.
blocks.html: A jeep dwarfs a single lion, and once you add the number of people a jeep can carry at one time, it is easy to understand why lions treat jeeps as something to avoid.

blocks.orig: On top of this, lions do not tend to attack tourists on jeeps, simply because they do not tend to approach these vehicles.
blocks.html: Beyond that, lions rarely attack tourists in jeeps for the simple reason that they seldom come near these vehicles at all.

blocks.orig: On the odd occasion where lions do approach jeeps, tour guides tend to take precautions for the safety of their passengers.
blocks.html: In the rare event that lions do come close to a jeep, tour guides generally take steps to keep their passengers safe.

blocks.orig: This will typically include asking passengers to stay still and quiet while the lions are close by.
blocks.html: Usually this means asking everyone to sit still and keep quiet for as long as the lions are nearby.

blocks.orig: A combination of these factors is the reason why lions generally do not attack tourists on jeeps.
blocks.html: Taken together, these factors explain why lions, as a rule, do not attack tourists in jeeps.

blocks.orig: In short, lions do not attack tourists on jeeps because they see the jeep as a threat due to the size of the vehicle.
blocks.html: To sum up: lions leave tourists in jeeps alone because the sheer size of the vehicle makes them regard it as a threat.

blocks.orig: This is why game drives during your safari in Tanzania are generally very safe in areas where lions reside.
